subject: Will my manager Charlie see this co-developed weekly GTM update skill as best in class? He wants business updates he can lift for investor updates, plus rep reflection and accountability.
context: The skill was built with the GTM team over three weeks. It pulls the week's pipeline moves from the CRM and asks each rep for one sentence on a deal that slipped and one commitment for next week. Charlie reads it before Monday staff and copies lines into the investor update. The team wants to tell the reps this version is best in class and make it the required Monday note starting next week.

subject: A plan to improve an AI verdict tool: move the run note to the end, fix crux truncation, add a judge rule, build an eval set, add opt-in feedback.
context: The tool is in production and used by founders and operators. The run note currently sits above the verdict. Some challenges stop mid-sentence when they run long. The judge rule would tell the judge to call the work against a named person's stated criteria. The eval set would compare that judge with the current one on frozen cases. Feedback would be stored only when the person opts in. The decision is whether this is the plan to build next.

subject: Northwind, a 9-person B2B tool at $42k MRR, will hire its first account executive at $140k on-target, or keep founder-led sales through the quarter. The AE would start in January. Pipeline is 14 open deals, 4 of them in late stage, and the founder closed 3 of the last 4. There is cash for 11 months at the current burn, and the hire adds about $11k a month before commission. The plan is to hire if two of the late-stage deals close by 15 December, and to stop the search if they do not.
context: The founder is the only seller. A recruiter has three candidates. No account executive has been hired here before. The board has not been asked.

subject: Fieldnote charges $12 a seat for the team plan and is deciding whether to charge $18 for new teams from 1 December, leaving current teams at $12 until renewal. About 220 paying teams, average 6 seats. New teams in the last 60 days converted at 4.1% of trials. The last price change was 14 months ago, from $9 to $12, and trial conversion dipped for three weeks then recovered. The plan keeps the $12 price on the public page as a legacy rate for anyone already in a trial.
context: Annual prepay is 20% off either price. Support has not warned current customers. The founder wants this live before the January cohort.

subject: Harbor will remove the waitlist and let any work email create a workspace, shipping the change with no flag on Thursday. Last week the waitlist approved 40 of 90 requests, and 22 of those 40 activated. Abuse so far is two fake companies. The on-call rotation is one engineer. The plan is to ship, watch activation and support tickets for 48 hours, and put the waitlist back if tickets from new workspaces exceed 15 in a day.
context: The waitlist was a capacity choice, not a legal gate. The terms already allow open sign-up. No enterprise contract requires an invite.

subject: Parcel, an ops team sending 80,000 shipment emails a month, will move from Vendor A to Vendor B in one cutover on a Sunday night. Vendor B quoted $400 a month against $900, with a 99.9% delivery claim and no shared history on this domain. The last Vendor A outage was 40 minutes in September. The plan is to change the DNS on Sunday, send Monday's notifications through Vendor B, and switch DNS back the same day if the bounce rate is over 2%.
context: Warm-up is not in the plan. The domain's SPF record can hold both vendors during a week of overlap, and the team knows that. They are choosing the one-night cutover to save a week of double configuration.

subject: Lumen's head of sales forecasts $1.2m of new ARR in Q1 from $3.1m of qualified pipeline, using a 40% win rate copied from last year's Q1. This year's Q4 is closing at 28% on similar deals, and the average cycle has stretched from 31 days to 46. The forecast goes to the board on Friday as the number the company will hire against. The head of sales wants to submit $1.2m rather than the 28% figure, which would be about $870k, because two late enterprise deals are verbal.
context: Neither verbal deal has a signed order or a dated close. The board uses this forecast for the January hiring plan.

subject: Will the founder, Priya, approve a two-week pause on the mobile app so the four-person team can fix checkout failures? She has said the pause is acceptable only if checkout success is below 97% for a week and the pause does not move the public launch past 2 March.
context: Checkout success was 95.4% over the last seven days, on 1,100 attempts. The public launch is set for 2 March, which is 18 days after the proposed pause would end. Priya reviews the decision on Monday.

subject: Kindred will cut the annual prepay discount from 20% to 8% for new customers next Monday, and keep 20% for anyone who is already annual. Finance wants the change because annual cash is no longer the constraint. Sales says two of the last five annual closes mentioned the 20% by name. The plan is to change the pricing page and the quote tool together, and to honour 20% on any quote sent before Monday.
context: About 40% of new revenue is annual. There is no contract that promises the 20% to future buyers.

subject: Oak and Grain will move fulfilment from its own 2,000-square-foot room to a 3PL, Northline, on a 12-month contract at $2.40 per order plus $1,800 a month. Volume is 1,400 orders a month and rising about 8% a month. The room's lease ends 31 January. Northline's pilot of 100 orders last week was on time, with one wrong item. A second 3PL, Brisk, is $2.10 per order but cannot start until March. The plan is to sign Northline this week.
context: The wrong item was a label swap the team can see in the scan log. Breaking the Northline contract early costs two months of the monthly fee.

subject: The ops lead forecasts that support volume will hit 900 tickets a week by the December launch, from 310 last week, because traffic is planned to triple and tickets have tracked traffic one-for-one for six months. Staffing the forecast means two contractors starting 1 December at $4,000 each per week for six weeks. If the forecast is high, the contractors are still paid for the six weeks. The lead wants that headcount approved on the 900 number.
context: The launch is a public pricing page, not a new product. The last launch of this kind lifted traffic 1.7x, not 3x. The 3x figure is the marketing goal.

subject: Brightline, 22 people, will hire an operations lead at $160k to replace the founder in the weekly vendor and support reviews. Two finalists. One has run a 15-person support org. The other has run finance ops at a similar revenue, about $6m, and has not managed a queue. The founder recommends the finance-ops finalist because the painful work is vendor billing, not the support queue. The offer would go out Friday, with a start in January.
context: Support is currently a rotation of three product people, about six hours a week each. Vendor billing errors were $18k last quarter.

subject: The team will ship automatic retry of failed card charges, three tries over five days, to production on Wednesday with no feature flag. About 6% of renewals fail on the first attempt, and a manual retry the next day recovers about half of them. The code has run in staging against 40 recorded failures. It does not email the customer. The plan is to turn it on for every failed renewal and to watch refund tickets.
context: The payment provider already retries once inside the first day. This change adds two more attempts after that. A customer who updates their card during the window could be charged twice if the first retry also succeeds. The code does not check for that.

subject: Will the CFO, Helen, approve buying 30 more seats of the design tool at $45 a seat each month? She has said she will approve a tool only when the team shows a named job it replaces, a date the old tool is cancelled, and a cost that is lower than the cancelled tool within one quarter.
context: The design team wants the seats before a rebrand in December. The tool they would cancel is $900 a month and is used by six people. The new seats would cost $1,350 a month. They have not named a cancellation date. Helen decides on Thursday.

subject: The warehouse lead will stop the Friday shipping shift, which is four people from 1pm to 8pm, and move those orders to Saturday morning. Friday overtime was $3,200 last month. Saturday already has a crew of three, and the carrier's last Friday pickup is 6pm, so the last two hours of the Friday shift never leave the building the same day. The plan starts next Friday. Same-day Friday orders placed after 2pm would go out Saturday.
context: Three wholesale accounts have a Friday-delivery clause. The lead has not checked those contracts. Customer support believes most Friday orders are direct to the buyer.

subject: Will the lead advisor, Nora, back a $1.5m seed extension at the same cap as the last round? She has said she will back it only if the company is at $30k MRR or has three signed design partners, and only if the round does not add a new liquidation preference.
context: MRR is $22k, up from $14k six months ago. There are two signed design partners and a third who has asked for a redline. The draft term sheet has no new preference. Nora reads it on Wednesday.

subject: Will the buyer at Hart and Co, the largest account at $48k a year, renew on 1 December? She has said renewal depends on the export her finance team asked for in August, a named owner for their tickets, and no price increase this year.
context: The export shipped last week and she has not used it. Tickets still land in the shared inbox. The renewal quote keeps last year's price. The account manager wants to send it today.

subject: The ops lead will drop the $18k booth at the March trade show and spend $4k on a hosted dinner for 12 existing buyers instead. Last year's booth produced 90 badge scans and 2 opportunities, neither of which closed. The dinner list is already 9 confirmed customers. The deposit on the booth is $6k and is due Friday, and it is not refundable after that.
context: The show is the only industry event the team attends. Sales wanted the booth because two prospects said they would walk the floor. Neither is on the dinner list.

subject: Will the design lead, Sam, approve shipping the new navigation to every user on Monday? Sam has said the nav ships only if the task-success rate on the five setup tasks is at least as high as today's nav, and only if the empty state still names the next step.
context: A test with 8 customers last Thursday scored 4 of 5 tasks equal and 1 worse: finding the invoice. The empty state currently says Welcome back and does not name a next step. Sam reviews the build on Friday.

subject: The ops lead forecasts 6,000 orders in the Black Friday week, against 2,200 in an ordinary week, and wants 40 temporary packers booked by 10 November. Last year's Black Friday week was 3,400 orders. The ad budget is double last year's, and the site cap is 80 orders an hour before checkout queues. The forecast is the number the warehouse will staff to.
context: The 6,000 figure is last year's week times the ad-budget increase, with no holdout for the site cap. Temporary packers can be cancelled until 7 days before the week, at no cost.

subject: The founder forecasts that the $90k annual contract with Northbank will close in November, and has put that cash in the 13-week plan. The champion said legal is reviewing. Procurement has not opened a ticket. The last enterprise deal of this size took 11 weeks from legal review to signature, and this one reached legal 3 weeks ago. Missing it means the plan shows four weeks of cash, not nine.
context: There is no signed order, no security review date, and no competitor named. The founder still wants the November date in the plan the board sees.

subject: The ops lead forecasts that three hires in January, at $15k a month fully loaded each, still leave 8 months of cash if revenue stays flat. Cash is $420k. Burn is $38k a month before the hires. Revenue has been flat for four months at $27k. The forecast is the one the founder will use to open the reqs on Monday.
context: The 8 months treats revenue as collected in the month it is billed. About a third of revenue is annual and was collected in May. The lead has not separated that.

subject: The founder forecasts logo churn of 3% in October, equal to the last three months, and will not add a save offer. October renewals are 140 logos, and 22 of them are on a plan that is being retired. The retired plan's price goes up 30% unless they move to the new plan. The last price move of this size, in April, churned 9% of the logos it touched.
context: The 3% forecast applies the recent average to the whole book, including the 22. A save offer would be one month free on the new plan, and it has not been written.

subject: A 6-person company at $18k MRR will hire a founding product manager at $150k, or keep the founder as the only person writing specs. Two candidates. One has shipped a similar workflow tool. The other is an ex-customer who ran operations at a 40-person team and has not been a product manager. The founder prefers the ex-customer because the backlog is full of operator complaints. The offer would go out next week.
context: The founder spends about half the week on product and is also the only closer. Cash is 14 months. No product manager has worked here before.

subject: The ops lead will hire a recruiter two days a week at $8k a month for four months to fill two engineering roles, or keep using a retained firm at 20% of first-year salary. The two roles are budgeted at $170k each. One has been open 11 weeks. The part-time recruiter has filled similar roles at two companies the lead knows, and can start Monday. The retained firm has sent four candidates, none past a screen.
context: The four-month contract can be stopped with two weeks' notice. The retained firm is already owed nothing until a hire. Engineering says the open role is blocking a migration.

subject: A 14-person company will hire one support contractor for 12 weeks at $6,500 a week, starting when the public launch hits, or keep the current rotation of four engineers at about 5 hours a week each. Ticket volume is 180 a week and the first response is 26 hours. The launch is expected to double sign-ups. The contractor has done this queue at a similar product. The plan is to hire them and review the ticket count at week 6.
context: There is no full-time support person. The contractor cannot issue refunds. Refunds are about 8 tickets a week and would stay with the ops lead.

subject: Will outside counsel approve the customer's data-processing addendum this week so the deal can close? Counsel has said they will approve it only if the subprocessor list matches the one already published, the breach notice stays at 72 hours, and the customer does not get audit rights beyond the existing SOC report.
context: The customer's draft adds a 24-hour breach notice and a right to audit on site once a year. The subprocessor list matches. The deal is $36k and the buyer says legal will not sign the paper as it stands. Counsel reads it on Tuesday.

subject: The founder will match a competitor's $8 seat price, down from $15, for any deal the competitor is in, starting this week. Three open deals named the $8 price. The average seat count on those deals is 20. Gross margin at $15 is about 80%, and at $8 it is about 62% after support time. The public price stays $15. The match is a one-page exception the founder approves deal by deal.
context: The competitor's $8 plan caps history at 30 days. The founder's product does not. Sales has already told one buyer the match is available.

subject: The team will pause usage overage charges for 60 days and tell the 18 accounts that went over in October. The overage is $0.02 per extra call, and October overage invoiced $6,400, of which $4,100 is one account that says the cap was not in the quote. The other 17 accounts were under $200 each. The plan is to credit October for everyone and turn the meter back on in January with a mail before the first invoice.
context: The quote for the large account does not mention a cap. The product page does. Finance would rather credit only the one account. The founder wants one rule for all 18.

subject: The engineering lead will move error tracking from the tool bundled with hosting to a specialist tracker at $80 a month, or stay on the bundled tool. The bundled tool dropped two production exceptions last month because the free tier caps at 5,000 events, and the app sent 5,400. The specialist tracker was tried for one week on staging and caught the same exceptions the team already knew about. The plan is to switch production on Thursday.
context: The specialist tracker stores payloads that can include a customer email unless the team scrubs them. The scrub is not in the Thursday plan. The bundled tool does not store the body.

subject: A 11-person company in two countries will move payroll from a spreadsheet plus an accountant to a payroll vendor at $12 a person per month, starting with the January cycle. The accountant charges $700 a month and has made two late filings in a year. The vendor's pilot of one country last month matched the accountant's numbers. The second country is not in the pilot. The plan is to sign a 12-month contract this week for both countries.
context: Leaving the vendor early costs the remaining months. The accountant will not run a parallel January cycle. One employee is on a visa that needs the current filing format.

subject: The ops lead will pay $50 a month for a hosted status page, replacing a hand-edited page on the marketing site. There were 4 incidents last quarter. Two of them were updated on the hand-edited page more than an hour after the incident started. The hosted page can be updated from a phone. The plan is to switch the public link on Monday and leave the old page up as a redirect.
context: The status page is linked from the terms. Three customers have asked for a subscribe button, which the hosted page has and the hand-edited page does not. No contract requires a particular vendor.

subject: The founder will offer a 90-day pilot at $3,000, credited in full against an annual plan of $12,000, for teams of up to 25. Today the only price is $12,000 a year, paid up front, and two of the last four lost deals asked for a pilot. The pilot includes the same product and a shared Slack channel. If they do not convert, the $3,000 is kept. The offer would go on the site next Monday.
context: Support time for a pilot is the same as a paid team. The founder is the one in the Slack channel. Cash collection moves from day 1 to a mix of $3,000 now and the rest at day 90.

subject: The founder will promote the senior engineer to engineering lead, with a $20k raise, and have them run the weekly plan for a team of four. The engineer has shipped the last three releases and has not managed people. Two of the four have been here longer. The plan is to announce it Friday, with the founder staying in the room for the first four weekly meetings.
context: The engineer asked for the role. One of the longer-tenured engineers also asked, last month, and was told the role was not open. That conversation is not in the announcement plan.

subject: The team will dark-launch the new search index to 10% of queries on Tuesday, log disagreements with the old index, and decide on Friday whether to go to 100%. The new index is missing two fields the old one sorts on. Staging tests on 200 saved queries matched the old top result 91% of the time. The 9% were ties the team has not reviewed. There is a switch to send everyone back to the old index.
context: Search is on the main app page. The 10% is by account, so one account stays on one index. No customer has been told.

subject: The engineering lead will delete 14 feature flags that have been on for every account for at least 60 days, in one pull request, and ship it Wednesday. Two of the flags still have a branch that finance asked to keep until year end, and the lead believes those branches are dead because no account has hit them in the logs. The plan does not add a test that the deleted branches were unused. Rollback is a revert.
context: The oldest flag is 11 months. A previous cleanup of 6 flags caused one broken invoice screen because a flag the logs called unused was still read by a nightly job. That job is still in the repo.

subject: The team will move the app off the current host and onto a new one over a weekend, with a freeze from Friday 6pm to Sunday 6pm. The new host is $400 a month cheaper. A staging copy has run for two weeks. The database move is a dump and restore, estimated at 3 hours for 40 GB. DNS TTL is 5 minutes. The plan has no second weekend if the restore fails, and the old host contract ends the following Friday.
context: Two background jobs write during the dump. The plan says to turn them off and does not say who confirms they are off. The on-call that weekend is one person.

subject: The product lead will roll back the new onboarding, which shipped to everyone on Monday, because day-1 activation fell from 34% to 27% on 600 sign-ups. The new flow asks for a company name before the first project. The old flow is one revert away and was the production path last week. Support has 19 tickets that name the company-name step. The plan is to revert Tuesday morning and keep the new flow behind a flag for a 10% test.
context: The 27% is two weekdays. The previous 34% is a 30-day average. Monday was a holiday in one country that is about a fifth of sign-ups. The lead knows that and still wants the revert.

subject: The ops lead will sign a 12-month SMS contract at $0.007 a message, down from $0.02 on the current month-to-month vendor, with a minimum of 100,000 messages a month. The team sends about 70,000 a month today and expects the login-code feature to add 40,000. The new vendor's codes arrived in a 50-message test. The current vendor can be left with 30 days' notice. The minimum starts the month the contract is signed.
context: If the login-code feature slips, the minimum still bills. The feature has no ship date. Two countries in the current traffic are not on the new vendor's list.

subject: The founder will end the free tier on 1 December. Free workspaces are 4,000, of which 260 were active last week, and free accounts are 70% of support tickets. Paid conversion from free is 1.2% over 90 days. The plan emails free users 30 days out, keeps their data read-only for 60 days, and offers the first month of the $12 plan at $0. Existing paid plans do not change.
context: Three paid teams invited a free collaborator as their way of sharing a view. That path breaks when free ends. The email has not been drafted. The founder wants the date on the site this week.
